title: unity_catalog: ATTACH ignores a named secret unless it names it
verdict: use an unnamed secret, or ATTACH ... (SECRET name)
description: `ATTACH '<catalog>' AS x (TYPE unity_catalog)` uses only the default (unnamed) `unity_catalog` secret. With a named secret (`CREATE SECRET uc (TYPE unity_catalog, ...)`) and no `SECRET` option, it does not fail on the missing secret: it requests the API with an empty endpoint, `/api/2.1/unity-catalog/...` with no host, and fails with `Could not resolve hostname`.

Workaround: create the secret without a name, or name it in the ATTACH: `(TYPE unity_catalog, SECRET uc)`. The endpoint is the server's root (`http://host:port`, with or without a trailing slash): one with the API path gets the path twice (404), and one without a scheme is refused (`Unsupported URL scheme`).

provenance.checked_by: homelab catalog session (AlexanderNenninger/homelab#9): DuckDB 2.0.0 in Python, extensions unity_catalog cc59382f52, delta 9dcfb65b99, httpfs 77392a7207, against Unity Catalog OSS 0.7.0 with unitycatalog/unitycatalog#1959 on MinIO

evidence.sql: CREATE SECRET uc (TYPE unity_catalog, TOKEN 'none', ENDPOINT 'http://unitycatalog:8080/', AWS_REGION 'us-east-1'); ATTACH 'homelab' AS lake (TYPE unity_catalog)
evidence.observed: IO Error: Could not resolve hostname error for HTTP GET to '/api/2.1/unity-catalog/schemas?catalog_name=homelab'

evidence.sql: the same named secret; ATTACH 'homelab' AS lake (TYPE unity_catalog, SECRET uc)
CREATE SECRET (TYPE unity_catalog, ..., ENDPOINT 'http://unitycatalog:8080'); ATTACH 'homelab' AS lake (TYPE unity_catalog)

evidence.observed: Failed to initialize curl URL: Unsupported URL scheme

provenance.notes: A first reading blamed the missing trailing slash; the same session's check of each combination showed the secret's name was the cause.
